headline: All seven majors sit on a green monthly candle and a red weekly one, and the tape can't decide which timeframe matters
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's cleaner than it looks at first glance. Five of seven majors, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, and BNB, hold above their 200-day lines with golden crosses intact. DOGE and ADA sit below theirs. That's a market with a majority trend still up on the long horizon, but the last week has been rough for all seven at once: BTC down 5.5%, ETH down 4.3%, SOL down 8.7%, XRP down 9.3%, ADA and DOGE both down over 12%. Zoom out to 30 days and the picture flips again, everything green, BTC up 18.5%, SOL up nearly 32%. Three windows, three different stories. None of them is wrong, they're just different rulers.

Momentum is where the divergence gets interesting. RSI readings are clustered right around the 45-53 neutral band across the board, BTC at 49.4, ETH at 50.9, SOL at 49.2, nobody overbought, nobody oversold. But MACD is below signal on every single asset, including the ones still above their 200-day average. That's a trend that's resting or rolling over on the daily timeframe even while the longer moving averages haven't broken. When price is up on the month, flat on RSI, and negative on MACD, the read is a market that ran hard and is now digesting, not one that's accelerating.

Positioning tells a quieter story than the price action. BTC funding on OKX is 0.0028% per 8 hours (3.1% annualized), modest and positive, meaning longs are paying shorts a small toll to stay in the trade, nothing close to overheated. ETH funding is actually negative (-0.1% annualized), SOL negative (-1.5%), XRP negative (-2.5%), which means short positions are the ones paying up on those three. DOGE stands out at 11% annualized funding with a long/short ratio of 4.66, the crowd is heavily long there and paying for the privilege, and DOGE liquidations over the last 15 hours are almost entirely longs ($383,536 wiped versus just $3,066 of shorts). That's a fragile setup on a token already 71.7% off its 12-month high. BTC open interest is largest at $2.15B with a long/short ratio of 1.82, and BTC longs also took the bigger liquidation hit over the last 2 hours ($277,879 versus $98,560 in shorts), a small tax on the optimists, not a rout.

Flows are where the tension sharpens. BTC spot ETFs printed a $450.4M outflow on Sep 15, and the five-session net is a $706.6M outflow, same direction both windows, a real signal. ETH ETFs pulled $142.3M out on the same day, but the five-session net is a $200M inflow, an outright disagreement between the daily print and the weekly trend, worth sitting with rather than smoothing over. Whale wallets, meanwhile, sent $164.6M net onto exchanges over the last 48 hours, driven mostly by ETH ($189.8M onto exchanges, largest single moves into Coinbase Institutional and Coinbase proper). BTC's whale flow was nearly flat (-$3.4M, essentially a wash between Binance inflow and Kraken outflow). Looking at the weekly whale series, three of the last four weeks (Aug 26, Sep 09, Sep 16) show net movement onto exchanges, which is coin heading toward venues where it can be sold, not away from them. Stablecoin float is up a modest 1.09% over 30 days to $309.5B, dry powder building slowly rather than surging.

Sentiment sits at 51, dead neutral, right in the middle of its own 30-day range of 41 to 74. That's notable precisely because it's boring: the crowd isn't panicking despite a red week across every major, and it isn't euphoric despite green months across the board. The gauge has essentially shrugged while ETF flows and exchange-bound whale activity lean cautious. When the mood reading is flat but the money movement has a lean, the money movement is usually the more honest witness.

What to watch from here: whether BTC MACD crosses back above signal while price holds the 200-day, which would resolve the momentum/trend divergence in the bulls' favor; whether the ETH ETF five-session number flips negative to match its own daily print, ending that disagreement; and whether DOGE's crowded long positioning (4.66 long/short ratio, 11% funding) produces another lopsided liquidation event. Any of those would change what this tape is actually saying, without anyone needing to guess at what comes next.
